summary: Align M13 Python interpreter validation with spawnable host files: Windows accepts explicit PATHEXT suffixes without appending a second extension, lookup is case-insensitive by platform filesystem semantics, directories are rejected, and POSIX candidates must have execute permission.

pointers: PATHEXT lookup accepts extensionless explicit .exe and mixed-case suffix
POSIX PATH lookup requires executable permission

steps: Reviewed Issue #70 and current settings.ts PATH/PATHEXT logic. Froze the behavior against the same command form later passed to Node spawn.

Replaced exists-only checks with ordinary-file validation and POSIX X_OK validation. Windows now detects an existing PATHEXT suffix and tests the exact command instead of producing only .exe.exe/.cmd variants; extensionless names still expand PATHEXT.
Added deterministic Windows PATHEXT tests plus cross-platform directory rejection and POSIX executable-bit coverage, and wired the test file into the full pnpm test command.

evidence.target: Issue #70 current implementation and runtime spawn contract
evidence.note: Confirmed the false-negative path for commands already carrying PATHEXT and the existsSync directory false-positive.
Candidate prepared for PR CI; the connected local container cannot clone GitHub because outbound DNS is unavailable.

limitations: CI has not executed this Candidate yet; Windows and POSIX assertions must be read back from Actions before merge.
This patch validates host executability but does not add shell alias resolution; the runtime itself does not spawn through an interactive shell alias either.
